question: What does the lab's only native prime-field algebraic oracle (pkm-semaev: S_(m+1) plus the membership equations of PKM's isogeny tower, solved by F4 over the tower ring) cost on three Table B curves (fp16, fp18, fp20), cold whole pipeline, in S = GAE/sqrt(r) across the AGENTS.md 5a band at w = 0, 0.1 and 1, against matched rho.negation and the generic-track incumbent on the same targets? This is the first counted row of the prime-field algebraic track: it establishes the track's own baseline and reports its distance to rho. It tests no new method and licenses no improvement or parity claim.

claims.text: Every iso-* run verifies [d]G = Q, and on every (target, t) the F4 arm and its engine=exhaustive grid arm have identical targets_tried, relations_found and matrix_rank, with zero crosscheck disagreements in the xchk arms (relation-stream identity).

Distance remaining: the cheapest verified pkm-semaev m=2 isogeny arm on each curve costs X times matched rho.negation at w = 0, 0.1 and 1 (paired ratio of summed S, 95% cluster-bootstrap interval over the 8 targets of the curve); reported as a distance, not a pass/fail gate.
claims.if_supported: the algebraic track has a counted baseline on Table B curves at these sizes; later algebraic-track candidates ratchet against it
claims.if_not_supported: the row is not established (an admission check failed) and no algebraic-track baseline exists yet

claims.text: Context: the order of the best iso arm and the matched generic incumbent (inc-n*) across the band, read as ecbench band --ranks does: cheaper at every weight, or unresolved inside the band. Under AGENTS.md "Tracks of index calculus" the tracks may be ranked against each other on the same instances; neither ratchets the other.
Context: on the same system, the counted grid (engine=exhaustive) is the cost an algebraic engine has to beat; report F4 over grid S at each weight.

hypotheses.statement: On each Table B curve the cheapest pkm-semaev m=2 isogeny arm is at least 10^4 times matched rho at w = 0.1 (the F4 multiply-adds, priced at 0.1 GAE each, dominate the whole pipeline).
hypotheses.mechanism: Per-trial F4 work is 10^6 to 10^8 F_p multiply-adds at t = 4..6 (Q-D table), against about one GAE of walking per trial; at w = 0.1 each multiply-add costs a tenth of a group addition.

predictions.minimum_effect: best iso arm / rho-neg paired ratio of summed S at w = 0.1, lower 95% bound above 1e4 on every curve

data_seen.measured: k = 20 miniature, 2 targets, isogeny t = 6, m = 2: S = 42.4 / 1.9e8 / 1.9e9 at w = 0 / 0.1 / 1 against rho.negation 1.71 / 1.84 / 2.99 [pcc:unverified]
targets_tried 11692 and 14932, F4 multiply-adds 6.16e11 and 7.78e11, solve wall 823.5 s and 1022 s, peak RSS about 25 MB, 25 columns, 15 and 18 relations [pcc:unverified]
Q-D table, isogeny form, k = 20: F4 multiply-adds per target 5.23e5 (t=4), 3.96e6 (t=5), 5.55e7 (t=6), 7.46e8 (t=7); columns 9, 18, 25, 65 [pcc:unverified]

hypotheses.statement: Within t = 4..6 the cost at w >= 0.1 rises with t on every curve: F4 work per trial grows about 14x per step in t while the trials needed fall by less than 2x.
hypotheses.mechanism: Hit probability per trial is about 2c^2/N for c columns, relations needed are about 0.7c, so trials fall as 1/c while c grows by 1.4-2x per step; Q-D F4 work per trial grows 7.5x (t=4 to 5) and 14x (t=5 to 6).

predictions.minimum_effect: iso-t6-m2 / iso-t4-m2 paired ratio of summed S at w = 0.1, lower 95% bound above 5 on every curve

data_seen.measured: Q-D table, isogeny form, k = 20: F4 multiply-adds per target 5.23e5 (t=4), 3.96e6 (t=5), 5.55e7 (t=6), 7.46e8 (t=7); columns 9, 18, 25, 65 [pcc:unverified]

hypotheses.statement: At w = 0 the isogeny arms cost a small multiple of the matched generic incumbent, so the whole gap to the incumbent sits in the priced F4 work.
hypotheses.mechanism: At w = 0 only group operations are charged: about one walk step per trial plus the one-off aux-curve search, comparable to the incumbent's walk.

predictions.minimum_effect: iso-t6-m2 / matched inc paired ratio of summed S at w = 0 within [2, 10] on fp20 (calibrated on 5.4 = 42.4/7.92 at k = 20)

hypotheses.mechanism: The oracle decides every non-refuted system on the grid and counts budget_exceeded; a refutation is exact over F_p.

positive.not_applicable_reason: ecbench ic.pipeline cannot plant a known decomposition R = P_i +- P_j into a trial; there is no oracle-check command for pkm-semaev yet. The exactness checks that exist are C1 (F4 against the counted grid on every trial, identical streams) and recovery of a hashed public target by [d]G = Q. A planted-decomposition detector is an implementation gap recorded in BLOCKERS.md; until it exists the row is admitted without a positive control and says so.

null_population.description: trial points at which the grid over V^2 finds no decomposition; F4 must return a refutation on every one (zero false positives) and the F4 and grid arms must emit identical relation streams
null_population.generator: the walked trial stream of each iso execution, classified by the grid arm on the same system
null_population.why_n: every execution has more than 1000 trials (derived 910 to 40,717 per execution, README section 6); zero disagreements over 1000 non-decomposing points bound the rate below 0.3% (one-sided 95%)

power.note: 8 targets per curve; the minimum two-sided sign-test p over 8 pairs is 2/2^8 = 0.0078, below 0.05/4. The predictions are order-of-magnitude (1e4, 5x) against per-target spread of about 30% (derived from 11692 vs 14932 trials on two k = 20 targets), so the design resolves them; it does not resolve a 20% effect, and none is claimed.

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: 14 arms x 3 curves x 8 targets x 1 round in spec.json (336 executions); stop when every planned execution has a record

budget: ceiling of 46 pod vCPU-hours for the whole row (2-vCPU pods: run and in-job replay-all Job deadline 54000 s; independent-replay Job deadline 28800 s; derived expectation 25 vCPU-hours, README section 6), inside the approved D-EKS allowance of about 49 CPU-hours, and a USD 10 ceiling for builds, idle and retries (plan). If a deadline or the ceiling is reached the session is kept as interrupted evidence, the unfinished executions are reported censored, and nothing is re-run with a larger limit

preflight gate for spec-m3.json: run 2 targets of iso-t4-m3-chain before freezing it; if the measured F4 multiply-adds per target exceed 3e11 (about 400 s), spec-m3.json is not run and the row says the m = 3 cell is unmeasured
any C1 mismatch (F4 and grid streams differ, a crosscheck disagreement, a run that does not verify) or any non-identical replay voids every iso-* record of that session
an execution that reaches timeout_seconds is censored, recorded, and never re-run with a larger timeout

decision_rule.text: Admission (all must hold, else the row is not established): every iso-* run verifies; C1 holds (identical streams, zero crosscheck disagreements); ecbench verify --replay-all is identical in the job and on an independent host class; C-aa-iso and C-aa-rho counted ratios are exactly 1.000. Then C2 reports, per curve and weight, sum S of the cheapest iso arm over sum S of rho-neg with its 95% cluster-bootstrap interval as the distance remaining; the cheapest arm per curve is the one with the smallest sum S at w = 0.1, fixed by this rule, and all arms are reported. C3 reports the ecbench band --ranks order of that arm against the matched inc arm as cheaper at every weight or unresolved. C4 reports F4 over grid S. No result is called an improvement of the generic track, no result ratchets another track, and no parity claim follows from any outcome.
decision_rule.threshold: no pass/fail threshold on C-iso-rho (distance remaining, owner criterion 2026-10-15); H1 and H2 thresholds read as stated in the predictions
decision_rule.statistic: ratio of summed S over matched (target, round) pairs (ecbench compare), per curve
decision_rule.interval: cluster bootstrap over the 8 targets of a curve, 95%, 4000 resamples
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: ratio of summed S per weight
